approved_decisions.B1: Keep unknown, not_checked, unavailable, not_found, error, gap, conflict and stale as distinct meanings.
approved_decisions.B2: Use separate vocabularies for presence, availability, verification, confidence, freshness, conflict, quality, review and application.
approved_decisions.B3: Use the 14-section, 216-path structural field dictionary as the basis for the future JSON Schema.
approved_decisions.B4: Keep baseline, observations, one proposed resolution, human decision and application state separate.
approved_decisions.B5: Use record_approved and record_rejected as A2 workflow states to avoid HubSpot approval-state ambiguity.
approved_decisions.B6: Keep HubSpot Lifecycle, Lead, Deal, Ticket, Sample Request and Account Status values as external references only.
approved_decisions.B7: Use needs_owner_review without approved owner rules and block writes while workflow dependencies are unverified.
approved_decisions.B8: Keep the no-integration ceiling; reviewed records cannot enter sync states.
approved_decisions.B9: Keep A2 requalification signals separate from A1-produced numeric score revisions.
approved_decisions.B10: Keep future external-system IDs nullable and connector-controlled; null never proves no external match.

not_approved: field-specific evidence, confidence and freshness thresholds
